A heterogeneous union has a key only when every two of its arms, those of one heading group included, fix different literals on a key column (logical/props.ts unionProps), and the page compiler refuses a heterogeneous union without one (logical/order.ts). So the arms of a paged heading group are pairwise disjoint, and UNION ALL over them delivers what UNION does; a group of overlapping arms is refused before this code runs.

Without the check, R03 also removes an occurrence binding only some of the containment's target fields, each matched to the referring occurrence's variable. Every node is a set, and the containment gives every referring row a target row agreeing on all its fields, hence on those bound, so the occurrence remains a pure existence test the containment discharges and the region's set is unchanged.

derivedMigrationName (deploy/render/naming.ts) never reads one change twice: a theory field's column and a manifest column object (a stored tag's) are never the same column, and no identity is added, dropped, changed or retired at once, so leaving out the deduplication, or keying it by identity alone, names the same changes.

An empty list there (sql/print.ts): no statement builder makes an empty DELETE USING, UPDATE FROM, aggregate ORDER BY, window PARTITION BY or ORDER BY, index INCLUDE or locking OF list (an index model's include: [] is no AST), so printing one is unreachable.
A non-associative operator's left operand (sql/print.ts) parenthesized from two levels up instead of one: only more parentheses, which PostgreSQL reads to the same tree.

A connective's or construct's operand count (lower/conservative/expr/ops.ts): the validated DAG gives AND, OR, LEAST and GREATEST at least one operand, NOT one and BETWEEN three, so the count tests never decide.
